record.field: A practical bridge between buyer requirements and accountable supplier execution.

Clear requirements before supplier promises

LightLink organizes each sourcing request around the product, intended use, target market, quantity, quality criteria and delivery requirement. This gives buyers and suppliers one working reference for the next decision.

Evidence stays connected to the project

Supplier options, quotations, samples, inspection findings, approvals and delivery milestones remain traceable in Odoo. AI may organize and translate working information, while people approve commercial and quality decisions.

Built for repeat purchasing

The result is not only one shipment. Confirmed product facts, supplier history and operating decisions can be reused when the buyer repeats or expands the purchase.
Confirm scope, payee identity, currency, fees and payment milestones against an approved quotation or invoice.

Use only payment instructions issued for your approved project

Payment methods depend on the service scope, supplier arrangement, destination and transaction value. Your responsible contact will provide the approved quotation or invoice before payment.

Verify changes before sending funds

Do not rely on account details copied from a public page, forwarded message or an unexpected email. If payee or bank information changes, confirm it through a second verified contact channel before paying.

Keep the payment record connected

Reference the quotation, invoice, project and payment milestone so finance and operations can reconcile the transaction in Odoo.

Use guides and project lessons to prepare better requirements, compare suppliers and control purchasing risk.

Learn in the same order as the sourcing workflow

Start with the product and market requirement, then learn supplier discovery, quotation comparison, sampling, quality control, commercial terms and delivery planning.

The blog remains the publishing system for individual articles. The structured guides below organize those articles into repeatable learning paths.
A structured learning path for defining the product, validating supply, approving quality and planning delivery.

1. Define the commercial objective

Clarify who will buy the product, how it will be used, the target quantity, required margin, destination market and launch timing.

2. Turn the idea into a supplier-ready requirement

Record dimensions, materials, functions, packaging, labeling, compliance needs and the details that must not change.

3. Compare suppliers with consistent evidence

Compare quotations only after confirming scope, MOQ, lead time, sample conditions, payment terms and what each price includes.

4. Approve samples and quality checkpoints

Use the approved sample and acceptance criteria as the reference for production and inspection decisions.

5. Plan the commercial and logistics handover

Confirm carton data, trade terms, documents, shipment route and responsibility at every handover before dispatch.
Evaluate a sourcing partner by scope, evidence, conflicts, communication, controls and the quality of its project record.

Define what the agent is responsible for

Supplier discovery, supplier management, product development, quality inspection, consolidation and logistics are different scopes. Confirm which decisions the agent prepares and which decisions remain with the buyer.

Ask how information is verified

A useful partner separates supplier statements from observed evidence and records unresolved risks instead of turning them into unsupported guarantees.

Understand fees and incentives

Confirm service fees, supplier commissions, third-party costs and any other commercial relationship that could affect the recommendation.

Review the working record

Ask how requirements, quotations, samples, inspections, approvals and delivery exceptions are documented and handed back to you.
